players.product: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) anti-PD-1 therapy; intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157), jointly developed with Moderna

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: 2025 total sales were $65,011 million (2024: $64,168 million), of which pharmaceutical $58,142 million. Keytruda/Keytruda Qlex $31,680 million (+7%), Gardasil/Gardasil 9 $5,233 million (2024: $8,583 million), Winrevair $1,443 million (2024: $419 million), Capvaxive $759 million and Welireg $716 million (+41%); Animal Health sales $6,354 million (+8%). Segment profits were $45,754 million for Pharmaceutical and $2,131 million for Animal Health.

10-K: capital expenditures were $4.1 billion in 2025 ($3.4 billion in 2024), of which $2.5 billion in the U.S.; Merck plans to invest approximately $20 billion in capital projects from 2025-2029, more than $12 billion of which relates to investments in the U.S. Higher 2025 investing outflows included the acquisition of a facility from WuXi Vaccines.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$20 billion of capital projects 2025-2029 (more than $12 billion in the U.S.); 2025 capex $4.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K collaborations: Lynparza alliance revenue with AstraZeneca was $1,450 million (+11%). In August 2025 Merck and AstraZeneca amended the Koselugo terms, ending revenue and cost sharing in exchange for a $150 million upfront payment in 2025 and $150 million in February 2026, with $150 million possible in Q1 2027 and $100 million in Q1 2028 subject to AstraZeneca's annual election, $175 million of regulatory milestones (all triggered in 2025) and mid-single-digit royalties; Merck paid AstraZeneca $700 million of sales-based milestones in 2025, and potential future sales-based milestone payments of $2.0 billion are not accrued. None of the pending generic Lynparza applicants challenges the olaparib compound patent, which expires in September 2027, the earliest date the FDA can approve them. Lenvima alliance revenue (Eisai) was $1,053 million, Reblozyl royalties (Bristol Myers Squibb) $525 million (+41%) and Adempas/Verquvo alliance revenue (Bayer) $470 million (+13%), which Merck expects to decline in 2026 on the loss of U.S. market exclusivity for Adempas. Keytruda Qlex relates to a license agreement with Alteogen (net intangible $886 million). Intismeran autogene is co-developed with Moderna, sharing costs and any profits equally; Merck capitalized a net $236 million of shared facility costs.
quarterly_data.figure: Lynparza alliance revenue $1,450 million; Koselugo payments $150 million (2025) and $150 million (February 2026); earliest generic Lynparza approval September 2027
